Charles “Engine Charlie” Wilson, formerly president of General Motors, became U.S. Secretary of Defense in 1953 under President Dwight D. Eisenhower. At his confirmation hearing, Wilson said he could not conceive of a conflict of interest between his former corporate role and his new government position.

Allen Dulles led the Central Intelligence Agency from 1953 to 1961. He oversaw CIA involvement in covert operations and supported using technology and intelligence gathering in support of U.S. military objectives.

James Killian, a physicist and engineer, served as the first chairman of President Dwight D. Eisenhower’s Science Advisory Committee. He contributed to developing the U.S. missile defense system and advocated greater investment in science and technology research.
